answer.rationale: Write-path p99 has climbed over 90 minutes during known daily settlement peak with heavy writes, which is consistent with saturation; memory_b3 is the closest prior on headroom absorbing a peak without dropping writes, but it was pre-peak provisioning, so the archive must be checked before treating reactive capacity as equivalent. A release 2 hours ago is a real alternate cause (onset ~30 minutes after deploy), so memory_b1 is the other record to verify; I am not rolling back yet because causation is unproven and a write-path rollback at settlement peak could interrupt customer/settlement writes. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) are rejected: fail-fast would sacrifice customer writes, which violates the objective. Failover and read-replica routing are unmotivated: no regional signal, and the stated load is writes, not report/dashboard reads. Downstream settlement value is flagged. Capacity add is the intervention most likely to protect availability without discarding writes while the two archives are checked; confidence stays moderate because a bad release would not be fixed by headroom.
